claims.statement: According to the Kojiki, Susanoo is a kami who emerged from Izanagi’s nose during purification after a visit to Yomi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kojiki, Susanoo adalah kami yang muncul dari hidung Izanagi ketika ia menyucikan diri sesudah mengunjungi Yomi.
claims.quote: A kami introduced by (Kojiki) as having come into being from the nose of Izanagi no mikoto as he was performing ablutions (misogi) to rid himself of pollution encountered while in the underworld (Yomi).

claims.statement: The stories of Izumo feature in Japan’s early myths.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Izumo termasuk mitos awal Jepang.
claims.quote: The Izumo region and Izumo Oyashiro Shrine feature prominently in several of Japan’s earliest myths.

claims.statement: The Nihongi says Susanoo was born to Izanagi and Izanami.
claims.statement_id: Nihongi menyebut Susanoo lahir dari Izanagi dan Izanami.
claims.quote: In Nihongi, however, Susanoo is described as being produced by Izanagi and Izanami

claims.statement: Both accounts place Susanoo with Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi among the three noble children.
claims.statement_id: Kedua sumber menempatkan Susanoo bersama Amaterasu dan Tsukuyomi sebagai tiga anak mulia.
claims.quote: Both accounts describe Susanoo as one of a set of three kami known as the "three noble children," the other being Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi

claims.statement: Susanoo has been associated with wind and rain.
claims.statement_id: Susanoo dikaitkan dengan angin dan hujan.
claims.quote: Susanoo has been associated with wind and rain, but many elements of his personality remain unclear.

claims.statement: Susanoo was banished after causing Amaterasu to hide in the heavenly cave.
claims.statement_id: Susanoo diusir setelah menyebabkan Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua langit.
claims.quote: Susanoo ran amok and caused Amaterasu to hide herself away in the heavenly cave, for which offense Susanoo was again banished.

claims.statement: Susanoo defeated Yamata no Orochi and received the sword Kusanagi.
claims.statement_id: Susanoo mengalahkan Yamata no Orochi dan memperoleh pedang Kusanagi.
claims.quote: Susanoo defeated the serpent Yamata no orochi, received the sword "Kusanagi"

claims.statement: Susanoo agreed to slay the serpent in exchange for marrying the couple’s daughter.
claims.statement_id: Susanoo setuju membunuh ular itu agar dapat menikahi putri pasangan tersebut.
claims.quote: Susanoo agreed to slay the beast in exchange for permission to marry their daughter.

claims.statement: Izanagi is a primordial Shinto god believed to have helped create the islands of Japan.
claims.statement_id: Izanagi adalah dewa purba Shinto yang dipercaya ikut menciptakan pulau-pulau Jepang.
claims.quote: Izanami ('she who invites') and Izanagi ('he who invites') are the primordial gods of the Shinto religion who are believed to have created the islands of Japan

claims.statement: According to the Kojiki and Nihongi, Izanagi and Izanami are central to the world’s formation.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanagi bersama Izanami berperan utama dalam pembentukan dunia.
claims.quote: According to Kojiki and Nihongi, one of the two kami (together with his consort Izanami) principally responsible for the formation of the world.

claims.statement: The two kami stand on a heavenly bridge and stir the sea with a spear; its drips form Onogoro Island.
claims.statement_id: Kedua kami berdiri di jembatan langit dan mengaduk laut dengan tombak; tetesannya menjadi Pulau Onogoro.
claims.quote: According to the myth, the two kami first stood on the "floating bridge of heaven" and used a spear to stir the sea below, whereupon the brine dripping from the spear's point congealed and formed the island of Onogoro.

claims.statement: Izanami died as a result of giving birth to the fire kami.
claims.statement_id: Izanami meninggal akibat melahirkan dewa api.
claims.quote: Izanami died as the result of giving birth to the kami of fire

claims.statement: Izanagi followed Izanami to Yomi.
claims.statement_id: Izanagi mengikuti Izanami ke Yomi.
claims.quote: Izanagi, no doubt unable to live without his beloved wife, rashly followed her down into the underworld or Yomi

claims.statement: Izanagi sealed Yomi with a large stone and performed river purification.
claims.statement_id: Izanagi menutup pintu Yomi dengan batu besar dan menjalani penyucian diri di sungai.
claims.quote: On finally reaching the outside world, Izanagi blocked the entrance to Yomi with an enormous stone. Fortunate to escape unharmed from such a terrible place of darkness the god had to perform a cleansing ritual in the river Woto to rid himself of the impurities of the underworld.

claims.statement: During purification, Amaterasu emerges from his left eye, Tsuki-yomi from his right, and Susanoo from his nose.
claims.statement_id: Saat penyucian, Amaterasu lahir dari mata kiri, Tsuki-yomi dari mata kanan, dan Susanoo dari hidung Izanagi.
claims.quote: It was during these rituals that various gods were born: Amaterasu, the sun goddess, when he washed his left eye, Tsuki-yomi, the god of the moon, when he washed his right eye, Susanoo (or Take-haya-Susa-no-wo), the storm god, when he washed his nose

claims.statement: Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo are known as the three noble children.
claims.statement_id: Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, dan Susanoo dikenal sebagai tiga anak mulia.
claims.quote: the "three noble children" Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo were also produced at this time

claims.statement: Yōkai are supernatural beings and phenomena of Japanese folklore, including spirits and monsters.
claims.statement_id: Yōkai adalah makhluk dan gejala gaib dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, termasuk roh dan monster.
claims.quote: Yōkai (妖怪) are creatures and phenomena of Japanese folklore including spirits, monsters, and just about all things supernatural.

claims.statement: In Japanese folklore, yōkai includes legendary ghosts, monsters, and spirits.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, yōkai mencakup hantu, monster, dan roh legendaris.
claims.quote: In Japanese folklore, yōkai (妖怪) refers to legendary ghosts, monsters, and spirits.

claims.statement: Yōkai is a broad term with no precise English equivalent.
claims.statement_id: Yōkai adalah istilah luas yang tidak memiliki padanan bahasa Inggris yang tepat.
claims.quote: it is a broad and vague term with no real English translation

claims.statement: Yōkai may be depicted as humans with altered features, animals, plants, insects, or household objects.
claims.statement_id: Yōkai dapat digambarkan menyerupai manusia berciri berubah, binatang, tumbuhan, serangga, atau benda rumah tangga.
claims.quote: some resembling humans, for example, with altered features such as a long neck or three eyes. Others looked like strange animals, plants, insects, or household goods.

claims.statement: Yōkai culture appears in picture scrolls and multicolored woodblock prints.
claims.statement_id: Budaya yōkai hadir dalam gulungan gambar dan cetakan kayu berwarna.
claims.quote: This exhibition introduces Japan’s yokai (Japanese folkloric imaginary monsters) culture that extends to the present day through picture scrolls and nishiki-e (a multicolored Japanese woodblock print)

claims.statement: Yōkai, once feared, have also come to be viewed as friendlier presences.
claims.statement_id: Yōkai yang dahulu ditakuti juga kemudian dilihat sebagai sosok yang lebih ramah.
claims.quote: yokai seem to have gradually become less of a subject of fear and have come to be viewed as a more charming and friendly presence.

claims.statement: Yōkai appear in media including toys and films.
claims.statement_id: Yōkai hadir dalam media seperti mainan dan film.
claims.quote: as well as a diverse range of media, including toys and films.

claims.statement: Tsukuyomi is a male kami regarded as ruling over the night.
claims.statement_id: Tsukuyomi adalah kami laki-laki yang dianggap berkuasa atas malam.
claims.quote: The second of Izanagi and Izanami's "three noble children," and usually considered a male kami with rule over the night.

claims.statement: Tsukuyomi is a moon kami in Japanese mythology and Shinto.
claims.statement_id: Tsukuyomi adalah kami bulan dalam mitologi Jepang dan agama Shinto.
claims.quote: moon kami in Japanese mythology and the Shinto religion.

claims.statement: Tsukuyomi’s name is thought to relate to reading moon phases in the lunar calendar.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tsukuyomi diduga berkaitan dengan pembacaan fase bulan dalam kalender lunar.
claims.quote: The name tsuku-yomi is thought to be originally related to the lunar calendar, and refers to the "reading" (yomu) of the phases of the "moon" (tsuki).

claims.statement: According to the Kojiki and one Nihongi version, Tsukuyomi emerged when Izanagi washed his right eye.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kojiki dan versi Nihongi, Tsukuyomi muncul saat Izanagi membasuh mata kanannya.
claims.quote: According to Kojiki and an "alternate writing" in Nihongi, Tsukuyomi came into being when Izanagi washed his right eye as he was undergoing ablution.

claims.statement: The Nihongi gives Tsukuyomi the sea, while the Kojiki gives him the night.
claims.statement_id: Nihongi menempatkan Tsukuyomi atas laut, sedangkan Kojiki atas malam.
claims.quote: Tsukuyomi was entrusted by Izanagi with rule variously over the sea (Nihongi) or over the realm of night (Kojiki).

claims.statement: A Nihongi version says Tsukuyomi killed Ukemochi and was separated from the sun by Amaterasu, explaining day and night.
claims.statement_id: Versi Nihongi menyatakan Tsukuyomi membunuh Ukemochi lalu dipisahkan dari matahari oleh Amaterasu, menjelaskan pemisahan siang dan malam.
claims.quote: an "alternate writing" in Nihongi relates that Tsukuyomi originally resided together with Amaterasu in heaven, but after killing the kami of foods Ukemochi, he was condemned by Amaterasu as an "evil kami" and forced to live apart from the sun, resulting in the separation of day and night.

claims.statement: Tsukuyomi is worshiped at Tsukuyomi no Miya in Ise.
claims.statement_id: Tsukuyomi dipuja di Tsukuyomi no Miya di Ise.
claims.quote: Tsukuyomi is the object of worship (saijin) at the detached shrine (betsugū) Tsukuyomi no Miya of the Grand Shrines of Ise

claims.statement: Tsukuyomi is enshrined at Tsukiyomi-no-miya and associated with the moon.
claims.statement_id: Tsukuyomi dipuja di Tsukiyomi-no-miya dan dikaitkan dengan bulan.
claims.quote: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto is the deity of Tsukiyomi-no-miya / the Koutaijingu Betsugu.It is a younger brother of Amaterasu Omikami and is likened to the moon.

claims.statement: Tengu can be considered yōkai or kami.
claims.statement_id: Tengu dapat dianggap sebagai yōkai atau kami.
claims.quote: They are considered a type of yōkai (supernatural being) or kami (god or spirit).

claims.statement: In Japanese folk belief, tengu inhabit high mountain woodlands.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Jepang, tengu menghuni hutan pegunungan tinggi.
claims.quote: a tengu, the embodiment of powerful and usually malevolent spirits who, in Japanese folk beliefs, inhabit the woodlands of high mountains.

claims.statement: Tengu are usually portrayed with human bodies, wings, and sometimes talons.
claims.statement_id: Tengu biasanya digambarkan bertubuh manusia, bersayap, dan kadang bercakar.
claims.quote: They are typically represented as having human bodies, wings, and sometimes talons in place of hands and feet.

claims.statement: Karasu Tengu has a birdlike head and sharp beak; Ko no ha Tengu has a human face and very long nose.
claims.statement_id: Karasu Tengu berkepala burung berparuh tajam, sedangkan Ko no ha Tengu berwajah manusia berhidung sangat panjang.
claims.quote: The Karasu Tengu has a birdlike head complete with a strong, sharp beak. The Ko no ha Tengu has a human face, distorted by an enormously long nose.

claims.statement: Tengu are credited with great strength, flight, shape-changing, and possessing humans.
claims.statement_id: Tengu dikisahkan memiliki kekuatan luar biasa, terbang, berubah wujud, dan merasuki manusia.
claims.quote: They are credited with many powers, including supernatural strength and the ability to fly, to assume other forms, and to take over humans through possession.

claims.statement: Tengu are sometimes described as benevolent spirits protecting people or temples.
claims.statement_id: Tengu kadang digambarkan sebagai roh baik yang melindungi orang atau kuil.
claims.quote: Occasionally, however, tengu appear as benevolent spirits who protect certain individuals or temples.

claims.statement: Older tales portray tengu as enemies of Buddhism who trick priests or burn temples.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lama menggambarkan tengu sebagai musuh agama Buddha yang menipu pendeta atau membakar kuil.
claims.quote: portray tengu as enemies of Buddhism, setting fires at temples or tricking priests.

claims.statement: Tengu’s image changed; by the Edo period they were also enlisted to help find missing children.
claims.statement_id: Citra tengu berubah; pada zaman Edo mereka juga diminta membantu mencari anak hilang.
claims.quote: For instance, tengu were long thought to abduct children, but by the Edo period they often were enlisted to aid in the search for missing children.

claims.statement: Inari is a tutelary deity of rice cultivation and the five grains.
claims.statement_id: Inari adalah dewa pelindung budidaya padi dan lima jenis biji-bijian.
claims.quote: A tutelary deity of rice cultivation and the five grains.

claims.statement: People throughout Japan pray to Inari Okami.
claims.statement_id: Orang di seluruh Jepang berdoa kepada Inari Okami.
claims.quote: People throughout Japan pray to Inari Okami for these things

claims.statement: Shinto classics call Inari Uka-no-mitama-no-kami.
claims.statement_id: Kitab-kitab Shinto menyebut Inari Uka-no-mitama-no-kami.
claims.quote: In the Shinto classics Inari is desiguated as Uka-no-mitama-no-kami.

claims.statement: Five enshrined deities at Fushimi Inari Taisha embody virtues of Inari Okami.
claims.statement_id: Lima tempat pemujaan utama Fushimi Inari Taisha mewakili keutamaan Inari Okami.
claims.quote: These five pillars of Fushimi Inari Taisha are named for the great virtues of Inari Okami that they embody.

claims.statement: Inari belief has a close association with foxes.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan Inari berhubungan erat dengan rubah.
claims.quote: Inari faith also has a deep association with foxes.

claims.statement: In commercial regions Inari was linked to prosperity, and in fishing villages to fishing.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah perdagangan, Inari dipercaya membawa kemakmuran usaha; di desa nelayan ia dikaitkan dengan perikanan.
claims.quote: In commercial regions, Inari was believed to be the kami who ensured commercial prosperity. In fishing villages Inari was the kami of fishing.

claims.statement: Fushimi Inari Shrine connects the name Inari with an older expression for reaping rice.
claims.statement_id: Kuil Fushimi Inari mengaitkan nama Inari dengan ungkapan lama tentang panen padi.
claims.quote: “Inari” is short for “Ine nari” or “Ine ni naru” (reaping of rice).

claims.statement: Izanami is a kami who bore deities of the land and is associated with an earth-mother image.
claims.statement_id: Izanami adalah kami yang melahirkan dewa-dewa alam dan dikaitkan dengan citra ibu bumi.
claims.quote: As the kami responsible for the birth of various other kami representing the land and its contents, Izanami has strong connotations of an "earth mother" goddess.

claims.statement: Izanami and Izanagi are believed to have created Japan’s islands and given birth to many Shinto gods.
claims.statement_id: Izanami dan Izanagi dipercaya menciptakan pulau-pulau Jepang dan melahirkan banyak dewa Shinto.
claims.quote: Izanami ('she who invites') and Izanagi ('he who invites') are the primordial gods of the Shinto religion who are believed to have created the islands of Japan and given birth to many of the other Shinto gods or kami.

claims.statement: Izanami is Izanagi’s consort.
claims.statement_id: Izanami adalah pasangan Izanagi.
claims.quote: Consort of the kami Izanagi. The name Izanami has been understood in various ways

claims.statement: Izanami was burned giving birth to the fire god, then fell ill and died.
claims.statement_id: Izanami terbakar saat melahirkan dewa api, lalu sakit dan meninggal.
claims.quote: Burning her genitals as she gave birth to the god of fire, Izanami fell sick and then died

claims.statement: Izanagi followed Izanami to Yomi.
claims.statement_id: Izanagi menyusul Izanami ke Yomi.
claims.quote: Izanagi, no doubt unable to live without his beloved wife, rashly followed her down into the underworld or Yomi

claims.statement: Izanagi was shocked by Izanami’s decayed appearance and fled.
claims.statement_id: Izanagi terkejut melihat wujud Izanami yang membusuk, lalu melarikan diri.
claims.quote: was shocked by the putrefying appearance of his dead wife, whereupon he fled from the place

claims.statement: Izanami threatened to kill one thousand people daily, and Izanagi replied he would give birth to fifteen hundred.
claims.statement_id: Izanami mengancam akan membunuh seribu orang setiap hari, dan Izanagi menjawab akan melahirkan seribu lima ratus orang.
claims.quote: the dead Izanami threatened to kill one thousand persons each day, but Izanagi stated that he would respond by giving birth to fifteen hundred persons

claims.statement: Yuki-onna is a Japanese yōkai without a single definitive story.
claims.statement_id: Yuki-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang tidak mempunyai satu kisah tunggal.
claims.quote: The Yuki Onna is one of Japan’s most well-known and yet unknown yokai. There is no single story of the Yuki Onna.

claims.statement: The name Yuki-onna means snow woman.
claims.statement_id: Nama Yuki-onna berarti perempuan salju.
claims.quote: Yuki Onna uses the kanji 雪 (yuki; snow) + 女 (onna; woman) to mean Snow Woman.

claims.statement: Yuki-onna stories occur in snowy parts of Japan and have regional variants.
claims.statement_id: Cerita Yuki-onna terdapat di daerah Jepang yang bersalju dan memiliki variasi daerah.
claims.quote: Anywhere there is ice and snow in Japan you will find legends of the Yuki Onna, often called by some regional variation.

claims.statement: Yuki-onna is often depicted with white skin and a white kimono.
claims.statement_id: Yuki-onna kerap digambarkan berkulit putih dan mengenakan kimono putih.
claims.quote: She resembles a classic yurei, with snow-white skin and a white kimono. The kimono is usually described as a thin, summer kimono

claims.statement: In Hearn’s story, a woman in white blows her breath on Mosaku.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Hearn, seorang perempuan berbaju putih meniupkan napasnya ke Mosaku.
claims.quote: he saw a woman in the room,—a woman all in white. She was bending above Mosaku, and blowing her breath upon him

claims.statement: The woman spares Minokichi because he is young.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu membiarkan Minokichi hidup karena usianya muda.
claims.quote: But I cannot help feeling some pity for you,—because you are so young... You are a pretty boy, Minokichi; and I will not hurt you now.

claims.statement: The woman forbids Minokichi from telling anyone and threatens to kill him if he does.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu melarang Minokichi bercerita kepada siapa pun dan mengancam akan membunuhnya jika ia melanggar.
claims.quote: But, if you ever tell anybody—even your own mother—about what you have seen this night, I shall know it; and then I will kill you

claims.statement: O-Yuki reveals she was the snow woman Minokichi met.
claims.statement_id: O-Yuki mengaku sebagai perempuan salju yang ditemui Minokichi.
claims.quote: “It was I—I—I! Yuki it was! And I told you then that I would kill you if you ever said one word about it!

claims.statement: Kappa is an amphibious supernatural being and water spirit in Japanese folklore.
claims.statement_id: Kappa adalah makhluk amfibi gaib dan roh air dalam cerita rakyat Jepang.
claims.quote: Kappa (河童 river-child) is an amphibious supernatural monster and water spirit in Japanese folklore.

claims.statement: Kappa are among Japan’s well-known yōkai.
claims.statement_id: Kappa termasuk yōkai terkenal di Jepang.
claims.quote: Kappa are among Japan’s most famous yōkai.

claims.statement: A contemporary Japanese image shows kappa with green childlike bodies and round head dishes.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran Jepang masa kini menampilkan kappa bertubuh hijau seperti anak dan memiliki cekungan bundar di kepala.
claims.quote: Contemporary Japanese people typically visualize kappa as having green, hairless bodies shaped like that of a human child. They have smooth, circular dishes on their heads

claims.statement: Kappa are said to live in rivers and ponds and drag swimmers into the water.
claims.statement_id: Kappa dikisahkan tinggal di sungai dan kolam serta menyeret perenang ke air.
claims.quote: Kappa live in rivers and ponds, where they catch hold of the feet of swimmers, dragging them to a watery death.

claims.statement: Before the eighteenth century kappa were also seen as monkeylike or otterlike.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum abad kedelapan belas kappa juga dipandang menyerupai monyet atau berang-berang.
claims.quote: Kappa were also thought of as mammals like monkeys or otters until the eighteenth century, rather than reptiles or amphibians.

claims.statement: From the 1950s kappa were also portrayed as cute.
claims.statement_id: Sejak 1950-an kappa juga digambarkan sebagai makhluk lucu.
claims.quote: it was not until the 1950s that the creatures were portrayed as straightforwardly cute.

claims.statement: Contemporary depictions show birdlike beaks and turtlelike shells.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran masa kini menunjukkan paruh burung dan tempurung mirip kura-kura.
claims.quote: pointed beaks like birds, which are often yellow. On their backs, they have what looks like a turtle’s shell

claims.statement: Kappa are said to enjoy sumō but may harm defeated opponents.
claims.statement_id: Kappa dikisahkan gemar sumo namun dapat mencelakai lawan yang kalah.
claims.quote: In folklore, kappa are commonly said to enjoy sumō, and this may seem superficially charming, but not if they pull defeated humans beneath the water, or otherwise harm them.

claims.statement: Uzume is the goddess whose dance drew Amaterasu from the heavenly rock cave.
claims.statement_id: Uzume adalah dewi yang menari untuk menarik Amaterasu keluar dari gua langit.
claims.quote: The goddess who danced so as to lure Amaterasu from the heavenly rock cave.

claims.statement: In Japanese mythology, Uzume’s dance to draw out Amaterasu is linked with kagura’s origin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Jepang, tari Uzume yang memanggil Amaterasu dikaitkan dengan asal kagura.
claims.quote: According to Japanese mythology, the origins of kagura lie with a dance performed by the Goddess Ame-no-uzume-no-mikoto to bring out Amaterasu Oomikami

claims.statement: The Kojiki and Nihongi say Uzume experienced divine possession after Amaterasu hid.
claims.statement_id: Kojiki dan Nihongi menyebut Uzume mengalami kerasukan ilahi setelah Amaterasu bersembunyi.
claims.quote: Both Nihongi and Kojiki relate that after Amaterasu hid away in the rock cave of heaven, Amenouzume underwent divine possession (kamigakari)

claims.statement: Uzume’s actions made the kami laugh and drew Amaterasu out of the cave in curiosity.
claims.statement_id: Tindakan Uzume membuat para kami tertawa dan membangkitkan rasa ingin tahu Amaterasu hingga ia keluar dari gua.
claims.quote: This behavior drew amused exclamations from the other assembled kami, and attracted the curiosity of Amaterasu, who at last came out from the cave.

claims.statement: Uzume is regarded as a patron of performing arts and a negotiator with unfamiliar beings.
claims.statement_id: Uzume dipandang sebagai pelindung seni pertunjukan dan perunding dengan makhluk yang belum dikenal.
claims.quote: In addition to her role as patron kami of actors and other performing arts, Uzume is also viewed as having the role of negotiator with new, unknown beings.

claims.statement: Uzume was sent to meet and identify Sarutahiko.
claims.statement_id: Uzume diutus untuk menemui dan mengenali Sarutahiko.
claims.quote: sent her to confront and ascertain the identity of the kami Sarutahiko

claims.statement: Ota Shrine is dedicated to Ame no Uzume.
claims.statement_id: Kuil Ota didedikasikan kepada Ame no Uzume.
claims.quote: Ota Jinja Shrine is located approximately 800 meters to the east of Kamigamo Jinja grounds and is dedicated to Ame no Uzume no Mikoto

claims.statement: Ame no Uzume is worshiped as a deity associated with artistic skill.
claims.statement_id: Ame no Uzume dipuja sebagai dewi yang membantu keterampilan seni.
claims.quote: Ame no Uzume no Mikoto is primarily worshipped as a deity that helps improve artistic skills.
